question.worked_solution:
To solve the equation $2-3\sqrt{x}=-x,$ we raise both sides to the power of $2.$  This allows us to get rid of the radical, and gives us a quadratic equation that is easier to solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-3\sqrt{x} & =-x \\ -3\sqrt{x} & =-x-2 \\ 3\sqrt{x} & =x+2 \\ {(3\sqrt{x})}^{2} & =(x+2)^{2} \\ 9x & ={x}^{2}+4x+4 \\ {x}^{2}-5x+4 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}-x)+(-4x+4) & =0 \\ x(x-1)-4(x-1) & =0 \\ (x-4)(x-1) & =0 \\ x & =1,\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Remember that in square root equations, we should always check the obtained value(s) to ensure that they are actually solutions of the original equation.

- First, we check whether the obtained value $x=1$ is a solution of the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-3\sqrt{1} & \overset{?}{=}-1 \\ 2-3 & \overset{?}{=}-1 \\ -1 & =-1\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Indeed, the value $x=1$ does satisfy the original equation.

- Second, we check whether the obtained value $x=4$ is a solution of the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-3\sqrt{4} & \overset{?}{=}-4 \\ 2-6 & \overset{?}{=}-4 \\ -4 & =-4\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Indeed, the value $x=4$ does satisfy the original equation.

Therefore, the only solution of $2-3\sqrt{x}=-x$  are $x=1,\,4.$
